author: @MrAnayDongre

evidence.api_compatibility: No breaking changes. The CLI error message text changed (more helpful), and subcommand help text gained a footer line. Existing scripts, configs, and integrations are unaffected. No API contracts were modified.
evidence.documentation: The change is a UX improvement that makes the CLI self-documenting — users reading the error or running --help now see how to pass the API key. No external docs, release notes, or spec updates were needed. The behavior is documented inline by the error message itself.
evidence.manual_release_testing: No human manually exercised the new error message or the subcommand footer before merge. CI validates the auth-failure code path but does not confirm the human-readable text is correct. This is a user-visible change to CLI output that should be verified on a release candidate.
evidence.post_approval_commits: One commit (b711e20, "Remove the response body check from the 401 error") was added after the first approval (2026-11-09T07:53:33Z). It drops the `res->body.find("Invalid or missing")` condition from the 401 branch so the hint is shown for all 401s, not just the server's own message. This simplified the change, was suggested in @bitgamma's inline feedback, and the reviewer re-approved the final code. No new behavior, scope creep, or risk was introduced.
evidence.review: PR #4103 was reviewed by @bitgamma, who has CLI subject-matter expertise per docs/dev/contribute.md. @bitgamma submitted a CHANGES_REQUESTED review requesting minor edits, responded to each, and gave two approvals (first on 2026-11-09T07:53:33Z with "one last wrinkle and we are good to go", second on 2026-11-10T07:01:28Z with "LGTM. Thank you!"). CodeRabbit raised several suggestions across the 401 handling and footer logic; @bitgamma dismissed the more elaborate ones in inline comments (noting the body-check approach was unnecessary and fragile, and that a test pinning the footer text was over-kill). The review was thorough on the scope of the PR, though CodeRabbit's suggestions about distinguishing provider 401s and handling nested commands were left as future work.
evidence.security: No security concern. The change only touches CLI error messaging and help text. No credential handling, network behavior, permissions, or code execution paths were altered.
evidence.tests: The CLI API key smoke test (test/server_cli_apikey.py) exercises `lemonade status` against a server with LEMONADE_API_KEY and without, confirming the CLI fails. The subcommand help pointer test (test/server_cli2.py) checks that --api-key appears in subcommand help. The test no longer pins the exact error text (review feedback removed it), but still validates the overall auth-failure path. Full C++ CI (112/112 tests) passed. The author confirmed local testing against a server with LEMONADE_API_KEY. No Windows/macOS local testing was performed.

maintainer_todos.text: Start the server with LEMONADE_API_KEY set and run `lemonade status` without passing --api-key to confirm the error message names both --api-key and LEMONADE_API_KEY.

subject: Fix unhelpful API key error in the CLI (#4103)
summary: Changes the CLI 401 error message from "Forbidden by the server. Did you set the API key?" to "Unauthorized (401): the server requires a valid API key. Use --api-key KEY or LEMONADE_API_KEY." and adds a footer line to every subcommand's --help that points users to `lemonade --help` for the global --host, --port, and --api-key options.
verdict_reason: The CLI now prints a more helpful error message and help text, but the improvement was not manually exercised by a human before merge.
